description:
pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:80-87

```rust
pub fn insert(&mut self, log: CtLog) -> Result<()> {
    let expected: [u8; 32] = Sha256::digest(&log.key_der).into();
    if expected != log.log_id {
        return Err(Error::ParseError);
    }
    self.logs.insert(log.log_id, log);
    Ok(())
}
```

Doc:

> Inserting a log with a `log_id` already present overwrites the
> previous entry.

The return value `Result<()>` only discriminates "log_id matches
key_der hash" vs "consistency check failed". It does NOT tell the
caller whether they just silently overwrote a different log with the
same `log_id`.

This matters in two real scenarios:

1. Caller stitches Apple + Google + Cloudflare log lists together.
   Two sources may publish the same log under slightly different
   metadata (different description string, slightly different
   usable_from timestamp). Caller wants to detect duplicate
   submissions, perhaps merge metadata. Currently they cannot.

2. Caller is incrementally refreshing the log list: insert all new
   logs, then check `len` to spot net additions. Today the net count
   tells them nothing because `insert` may have overwritten existing
   entries.

`BTreeMap::insert` returns `Option<V>` — the previous value. This
crate's wrapper discards that information.

Fix: change signature to `pub fn insert(&mut self, log: CtLog) ->
Result<Option<CtLog>>` — Ok(None) for fresh insert, Ok(Some(prev))
for overwrite. The doc comment already states overwrite is the
behavior, so this is just exposing the information that's already
there. Non-breaking-with-deprecation if a separate
`insert_overwriting` accessor is added.

Actually fix earlier: add a separate `insert_unique` returning Err
if log_id already present, leaving `insert` to its current overwrite
semantics with the upgraded return type.

Priority P2: the contract is documented (overwrite happens) but
callers cannot detect or react to it. Defensive-forcing because
callers wanting overwrite-detection have to clone the prior list,
check membership, and clone the new list — wasteful.
title: CtLogList::insert overwrite semantics undocumented in return value — silent dropped logs
